title: The Autopsy of Bellwether Lane
premise: Retired detective Mirabel Okonkwo has spent six years hiding behind the counter of her failing bookshop, quietly untangling three deaths the police dismissed as accidents. When a missing woman's diary arrives anonymously—its entries continuing weeks past the date of her disappearance—Mirabel realizes the witness everyone believes dead may still be alive, and someone is willing to kill to keep it that way. As she follows the diary's coded references through Bellwether Lane's respectable facades, she uncovers a cover-up entwined with her own late husband's final case and must choose between protecting the people who shielded her and exposing a truth that will destroy them. In the end, Mirabel finds the living witness hidden in plain sight, trades her invisibility for justice, and reopens the bookshop under her own name.
about_author: Orsen Montrose is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent two decades transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about ordinary people who notice what institutions prefer to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A slow morning in the failing bookshop establishes her routines, her grief for her husband Edmund, and her unspoken habit of solving cold cases from her armchair. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. An anonymous parcel contains Hester Vane's diary—the same diary entered as evidence when Hester vanished four years ago—but the entries continue eleven days beyond her disappearance date. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Constable Knew
chapters.summary: Mirabel visits retired constable Dougal Reeve, who worked Hester's case and now drinks too much. He confirms the diary was logged closed on day one but goes pale at the later dates. POV alternates briefly to Dougal. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing.

chapters.title: Bellwether Lane After Dark
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She walks the lane where Hester was last seen, noticing a house with fresh paint over old damage. Someone watches her from an upstairs window. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she is also prey.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Hand
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with flashback. She reviews her three quiet solutions and finds a thread connecting all three victims to the Bellwether Lane residents' association. Emotional beat: pattern recognition as both gift and curse.

chapters.title: The Bookseller's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel decodes the diary's marginalia using books Hester bought from her shop; each title marks a meeting place. First entry points to the boathouse. Emotional beat: intimacy with a stranger through her own inventory.

chapters.title: Boathouse Water
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the boathouse she finds a weatherproof cache—photographs of a council bribery scheme—and is nearly caught by an unknown man. Emotional beat: fear she hasn't felt since active duty.

chapters.title: Dougal's Confession, Half-Spoke
chapters.summary: Dougal's POV. Pressured by Mirabel, he admits he falsified the timeline under instruction from above but refuses to name names. That night his flat is ransacked. Emotional beat: cowardice curdling toward courage.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mirabel interviews Councillor Ashworth's widow, Ivy, whose alibi contradicts the official record. Ivy recognizes Mirabel from Edmund's old case files. Emotional beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Edmund's Last Folder
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, flashback-heavy. She reopens Edmund's unfinished final investigation and discovers Hester Vane was his confidential informant. Emotional beat: love against duty—Edmund chose the case over safety, and died for it.

chapters.title: A Message in Secondhand Ink
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A customer returns a book with an inscription in Hester's handwriting dated last month: 'Tell the bookseller I'm counting pages.' Proof of life. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as commerce.

chapters.title: The Residents' Association Dinner
chapters.summary: Mirabel infiltrates the association's annual dinner, mapping alliances among Ashworth's old circle. She is recognized by solicitor Peter Grieve, who warns her off with unsettling gentleness. Emotional beat: menace wearing evening dress.

chapters.title: Pages Counted Backward
chapters.summary: Mirabel works out the 'counting pages' cipher: the diary's later entries encode a location—a disused chapel on the lane. Dougal agrees to watch her back. Emotional beat: trust cautiously rebuilt.

chapters.title: Chapel of Small Voices
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The chapel yields signs of recent habitation and a second journal—Hester's own account of the bribery ring. But they are followed; Dougal is attacked and hospitalized. Emotional beat: loyalty exacting its price.

chapters.title: The Man from Upstairs Window
chapters.summary: POV shifts to the watcher: private enforcer Callum Rhee, hired by Grieve to retrieve the journals without leaving bodies—yet. His orders change after the chapel. Emotional beat: a professional beginning to doubt his employer.

chapters.title: Grieve's Bargain
chapters.summary: Grieve confronts Mirabel in her shop, offering her silence-for-silence: he knows she solved the three 'accidents' and will bury her if she publishes hers. Emotional beat: duty versus survival laid bare.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Owes the Dead
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, night of decision. She reads Edmund's letters, weighs reopening the shop versus fleeing, and chooses truth—mailing copies of both journals to the press and police as insurance. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Witness in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Mirabel deduces Hester never left: she has been living as the reclusive archivist at the parish records office, face altered by injury. Their meeting is wary, tender, furious. Emotional beat: two women who hid for different reasons recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Fire on Bellwether Lane
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Grieve, exposed by the mailed copies, sends Rhee to burn the records office. Mirabel and Hester escape through the archive stacks as evidence burns around them. Emotional beat: terror and defiance intertwined.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Hester comes forward publicly; Dougal, discharged from hospital, corroborates the falsified timeline. Rhee, disgusted, hands over recordings of Grieve's instructions. Emotional beat: the cost of truth paid in full view.

chapters.title: The Verdict of Neighbors
chapters.summary: Grieve's arrest cracks the town open; the association dissolves; Ivy Ashworth testifies about her husband. Mirabel faces the community that preferred her invisible. Emotional beat: vindication that feels like loss.

chapters.title: Open Sign, New Name
chapters.summary: Resolution. Months later, the bookshop reopens repainted and renamed 'Vane & Okonkwo,' with Hester as partner. Mirabel keeps Edmund's folder framed behind the till. Final line echoes the first chapter's quiet—now chosen, not imposed. Emotional beat: peace earned, not inherited.
